 : JUDGMENT :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the Corrigendum passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator- Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru - Respondent No.2, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/07/2011-12 dated 09.03.2020 pertaining to Sy. No.24/3 measuring 4 guntas,
Sy. No. 24/4 measuring 25 guntas and Sy. No. 24/5 measuring A.P. No.98/2021 12 guntas, totally measuring to an extent of 1 acre 1 gunta of land situated at Byatarayanapura village, Bengaluru North Taluka.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the Sy. No.24/3 measuring 4 guntas, Sy. No. 24/4 measuring 25 guntas and Sy. No. 24/5 situated at Byatarayanapura village, belonging to the respondent No.1 has been acquired under Preliminary Notification bearing No. S.O. No. 1270(E)
published in the official Gazette on 05.12.2002 and Final Notification under Section bearing S.O.
No.829(E) was published in the official Gazette on 22.07.2003.

The respondent No.3 has passed the award and disbursed a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- as compensation towards 4 guntas of land in Sy. No.
24/3, a sum of Rs. 6,25,000/- towards 25 guntas in Sy. No. 24/4 and a sum of Rs. 3,00,000/-
towards 12 guntas in Sy. No. 24/5, altogether a sum of Rs.10,25,000/- has been awarded as compensation and the said amount has been disbursed to the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 received the said amount under protest and filed an A.P. No.98/2021 application for enhancing proper and fair compensation.
Accordingly, the said application is taken by the respondent No. 2 for consideration.

.3. In the said petition/proceedings before the respondent No.2, this petitioner filed statement of objections stating that the application filed by the petitioner for reference is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

The respondent No.1 has not produced any documents to establish that the value of the subject lands was more than what has been under sale deed dated 22.11.2010 and also not produced a single sale transaction of Rachenahalli village with the market value at Rs. 17,000/- or Rs. 18,000/- per Sq. feet.

Further, it is claimed by the petitioner that the proper compensation has been awarded by the respondent No.3 and claimed that the respondent No.2 has awarded excess amount than the market value of the property under Preliminary Notification.
The petitioner in the objection statement also stated about the provisions of law and case Laws and prayed for dismissal of the reference.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-07/2011-12 dated 09.03.2020.
In compliance of the order, the petitioner after deducting the TDS amount disbursed the enhanced compensation of Rs. 3,40,16,887/-.

After receipt of the the enhanced compensation, the respondent No.1 stealthily approached the respondent No. 2 on 06.11.2020 after the lapse of 8 months from the date of passing the award seeking modification of Arbitral Award dated 09.03.2020 claiming interest @ 9% on the award from 30.03.2004.

The petitioner claims that no notice has been issued to the counsel appearing for the petitioner in the main matter and also claimed that the petitioner has already disbursed amount with interest, as such, question of revision of interest does not arise.
Further it is stated that the petitioner after examining the records pertaining to the project informed the respondent No.2 that formation of road was carried out and completed during November 2005.
On the basis of the said details provided in the petitioner's letter dated A.P. No.98/2021 28.12.2020, the respondent No.2 passed the Corrigendum dated 05.01.2021.

The petitioner also claimed that the corrigendum order is not in accordance with law and the order is hit by Section 33(1) and (2) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act,
the advance notice has not been given to the petitioner and also claimed that the application for enhancement itself is barred by limitation and among other grounds prayed to set aside the corrigendum order dated 05.01.202.
.5.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Corrigendum to the Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the Corrigendum passed by the respondent No. 2 is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamental of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The petitioner claims that the respondents 1 and 2 have violated the provision of Section 33(1)(a) of the Arbitration and A.P.
No.98/2021 entertained the application of respondent No.1 contrary to the legal provisions and against the principles of natural justice.

The modification of the order regarding the payment of interest in the corrigendum is not in accordance with law and hit by Section 33 of the Act and also the said order is liable to be interfered as the same is not in accordance with law and among other grounds prayed to set aside the corrigendum order dated 05.01.2021.
.6.

The respondent No. 1 appeared through his counsel and filed detailed objection stating that the corrigendum order dated 05.01.2021 is in accordance with law, hence that cannot be set aside and among other grounds prayed for dismissal of the petition.
The respondent No. 2 has appeared before the Court through ADGP.

The respondent No. 3 though served with the notice, did not appear before the Court and h e n c e , p l a c e d e x p a r t e . T h e e n t i r e r e c o r d s i n A . P . N o . 9 8 / 2 0 2 1 LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/07/2011-12 secured from the Arbitrator.

.7. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is as under:

.8.
Heard the arguments.

The learned advocate for the petitioner relied on the judgments reported in (1) AIR 2020 SC 717 - The Executive Engineer, Nimna Dundha Project Vs. the State of Maharastra and others;
(2) AIE 2003 Karnataka page 165; (3) ILR 1985 Karnataka (SC) page 1261; (3)

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in the negative, for the following:
A.P. No.98/2021 REASONS .9.
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 M/s.
Ministry of Communication Employees Co-operative Housing Society Limited was the owner of the property measuring 1 acre 1 guntas of Byatarayanapura village, that has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 05.12.2002 and Final Notification dated 22.07.2003 is an admitted fact.

sentences.text: It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the 2 nd respondent vide award dated 09.03.2020 in No.LAQ/NH- 7/CR/07/2010-11 enhanced the compensation of the acquired land by determining the market value of the property.
The order passed by the respondent No. 2 in the award dated 09.03.2020 in the operative portion at para 1 and 2 is not in dispute.
In fact, the petitioner by accepting the said order also paid the compensation.
The disputed operative portion of the order in this case is at para No. 3 of the award dated 09.03.2020.

The said portion of the order reads as under:
"      9      ,      3  (5)   
     1    2             ."

The respondent No. 2 arbitrator in the award granted the compensation by ordering to pay the interest on the compensation at the rate of 9% from the date of handing over the possession of the acquired land till deposit of the amount to the petitioner.

.11. In the case on hand, the parties to the proceedings are not disputing that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation from the date of handing over of the possession of the acquired property till depositing of the amount.

Therefore, in the case on hand, it is clear that the order of the respondent No.2 is directing the petitioner to make the payment of interest at 9%

4 from the date of taking A.P. No.98/2021 possession of the acquired property till depositing of the amount.

sentences.text: It is also relevant to note that even according to Section 3(h)(e) of NHAI Act, the person who losses the property is entitled for interest on the compensation amount from the date of parting with the possession of property till the depositing/payment of the compensation.
The said is also admitted by the petitioner also.

Therefore, in the case on hand, the point to be considered in the case is that when actually the petitioner has taken possession of the property or the respondent No.
1 parted with the possession of the property.

.12. The award passed by the respondent No.2 at para No. 3 only disclose that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest from the date of handing over the possession of acquired property to the petitioner.
Hence, the court has to find out which is the date in which possession of the property has been handed over to the authority of the acquired land.
The learned Advocate for the specifically claimed that the petitioner has taken the possession of the property as on 30.06.2011.

In support A.P. No.98/2021 of the said contention, the learned Advocate for the petitioner relied on the acknowledgment given by the respondent No.1 as per Annexure - E produced along with petition at page No. 27.
It is true that the authorized person / president of the respondent No.1 put a date as 30.06.2011 after signing the said document.
The said document is regrading handing over of the possession of acquired property.
The entire case of the petitioner is based on this document and on the basis of the this document only, the petitioner claims that possession of the property has been taken as on 30.06.2011.

Hence, claimed that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation only from 30.06.2011 and not from 2004 as ordered in the impugned corrigendum.
.13.

Per contra, it is the case of the respondent No.1 that as there is an ambiguity regarding date of possession or it is not made known to the respondent No.1 regarding date of taking possession of acquired property by the petitioner, it has filed an application to clarify the same as per letter dated 06.11.2020 for A.P. No.98/2021 clarification regarding the date of handing over possession, so that there will be a clarity in the order.

The respondent No.1 further claimed that in pursuance of the said application, the respondent No. 2 / arbitrator sought information from the petitioner by writing a letter dated 27.11.2020 regarding the date of taking of possession of the acquired property.

In response to the said letter, the Project Director of the petitioner vide letter dated 28.12.2020 informed the respondent No. 2 / arbitrator that the work of widening the road has commenced in the year 2004 and the same has been completed in the month of November 2005.

In view of this reply by the project manager of the petitioner, the respondent No.1 claimed that the possession of the acquired property has been taken by the petitioner as on the date of award or as on 30.03.2004.
Accordingly claimed that on the basis of the reply given by the petitioner dated 28.12.2020, the respondent No. 2 passed the corrigendum order and it is in accordance with law.
In view of these rival claims of the parties, the Court has to examine the materials before the Court regarding the date of taking possession of the acquired property by the petitioner.
.15. In the case on hand, after registering the case, the Court call for entire records from the arbitrator.
On perusal of the records, the arbitrator passed the corrigendum order as on 05.01.2021.

sentences.text: The records of the Arbitrator at page No. 236 reveals that the respondent No. 1 submitted a letter to the respondent No. 2 praying to modify the order claiming that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest from the date of award passed as on 30.03.2004.

In the said application, the respondent No. 1 made out a case that it has received the compensation on 30.06.2011 and the work has been completed in the year 2005 itself and the respondent No.1 is entitled for compensation with interest from the date of taking of possession as per Section 3(h)(5) of NHAI Act.

In response to the said application of the respondent No.1, the respondent No.2 / Arbitrator has written a letter to A.P.
No.98/2021 the Project Director of the petitioner on 27.11.2020 requesting to furnish the particulars of taking possession of the acquired property.

In response to the said letter, the Project Director /
General Manager vide letter dated 28.12.2020 stated that the formation of road has been carried out in the year 2004 and completed during November 2005.

If this is accepted, certainly it has to be accepted that the possession of the property has been handed over to the petitioner for formation of road in the year 2004 itself, otherwise it is not possible for the petitioner to carry out formation of road work.

.16. At this juncture it is also relevant to note one more letter issued by Project Director of NHA dated 19.09.2020 to the Regional Officer, NHAI at page No. 8 paragraph No. 3 and 4 reads as Trial Court at page No.
40) "In so far as the subject matter is concerned, it appears from the documents that the award was passed by CALA on 30 th March 2004.
The award notices in respect of Sy. No. 24/3, 24/4 and 24/5 were issued on the very same day i.e., 30th March 2004.
But the compensation was disbursed on 30 th A.P. No.98/2021 June 2011 as it appears that the land loser approached CALA only on the said date with relevant documents to satisfy their titles.
In the instant case, it is an admitted fact that the possession of the lands was taken much prior to the execution of the possession certificate on 30th June 2011.

If work on the stretch of NH-7 itself was completed in 2005, utilizing the land acquired from the said Society, NHAI cannot take a stand that possession certificate was signed on 30th June 2011 and hence interest is payable from the said date.
We are of the considered opinion that interest is payable from the date of actual handing over of possession, which is intent of the law."
Therefore, the award has been passed on 30.03.2004, but the compensation was disbursed on 30.06.2011 and as on that date, the land loser approached with documents.

Hence, it is clear that till 30.06.2011 the land loser / respondent No. 1 not appeared before the petitioner and on that date, while making the payment, the signatures of the respondent No. 1 has been obtained on the documents.

It is also relevant to note that even the documents relied by the petitioner produced at Annexure - E does not specify the A.P. No.98/2021 date of handing over possession and the said date is kept blank.
If at all the possession of the property has been handed over on 30.06.2011 itself, certainly the said date would have been mentioned at Annexure-E.

The said fact certainly leads to draw inference that while making the payment of compensation as on 30.06.2011, the petitioner has obtained the signatures on the voucher for payment of compensation at Annexure-B and Annexure- E. .17.
Except Annexure-E, there is nothing on record to show that the possession of the property has been handed over to the petitioner as on 30.06.2011.

If at all the possession of the acquired property has been handed over to the petitioner as on 30.06.2011, it is practically impossible for the petitioner to commence the formation of road work in the year 2004 National Highways Authority Of India vs M/S Ministry Of Communications ... on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112216299/
6 and complete the same in the year 2005.

sentences.text: As such, the court left with no option than to accept that the possession of the property has been delivered to the petitioner much prior to 30.06.2011 and particularly in the year 2004 itself.

It is evident from the A.P. No.98/2021 observation of the letter dated 19.09.2020 by the Project Director at page 8 para 4 that the land loser / respondent No. 1 is entitled for compensation from the date of actual handing over of possession.
Further the burden is on the petitioner to show that when actually they have taken possession of the property.
The petitioner is failed to make out a specific case of taking possession of property.
Under such circumstances, the Court can safely infer that the date of award itself is the date of taking of possession of the acquired property.
.18. It is well settled principle of law that the land looser is entitled for compensation with interest from the date of handing over the possession.

The award passed by the respondent No. 2 dated 09.03.2020 at paragraph 3 reads as under:
"      9      ,      3  (5)   
     1    2             ."
A.P. No.98/2021
Therefore, even in the order, the Arbitrator made it clear that the respondent No.1 is entitled for interest @ 9% for compensation from the date of handing over the possession.
The clarity sought by the respondent No.1 is regarding the said date.

The Arbitrator after obtaining the explanation from the Project Director of the petitioner / NHAI passed the Corrigendum order and in the corrigendum order, the respondent No.1 only clarified regarding the date of handing over the possession which is in accordance with law.
.19 . The only dispute in the case is regarding passing of the Corrigendum or additional award or modification of award passed by the respondent No. 2 dated 05.01.2021.
The petitioner in this petition only challenged the said Corrigendum / rectification / additional award dated 05.1.2021 under the Heading "  ".

All these facts are evident from the petition averments,
wherein, the petitioner at para No. 3 of the petition specifically stated that "The petitioner being highly aggrieved by the Corrigendum dated A.P. No.98/2021 05.01.2021 to the Arbitral Award dated 09.03.2020 passed by the 2nd respondent, has preferred this petition".
The 2nd prayer in the petition reads as "Set aside the Corrigendum dated 05.01.2021 passed by the 2nd respondent in case No. LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/07/2011-12.

Hence, the only fact to be considered in this case is that whether Corrigendum or rectification award or additional award is in accordance with the law and whether that has been intervened by this Court.

.20. The counsel for the petitioner vehemently argued that the additional award or corrigendum is not in accordance with Section 33 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act and also claimed that there no notice has been given to the petitioner who is the aggrieved party before passing corrigendum or the impugned order.

Per contra, the 1st respondent claims that it is a correction or interpretation of award and the said correction is made in accordance with the evidence placed before the Arbitrator and it is accordance with law as well as the guidance A.P. No.98/2021 value issued by the National Highways Authority Of India vs M/S Ministry Of Communications ... on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112216299/

sentences.text: Hence, it is just and necessary to see whether impugned order amounts to correction or additional award or rectification of the award.

Hence, it is just and necessary to note Section 33 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, which reads as under:
"33. Correction and interpretation of award; additional award.

(1) Within thirty days from the receipt of the arbitral award, unless another period of time has been agreed upon by the parties-- (a) a party, with notice to the other party, may request the arbitral tribunal to correct any computation errors, any clerical or typographical errors or any other errors of a similar nature occurring in the award;
(b) if so agreed by the parties, a party, with notice to the other party, may request the arbitral tribunal to give an interpretation of a specific point or part of the award.

(2) If the arbitral tribunal considers the request made under sub-section (1) to be justified, it shall make the correction or give the interpretation within thirty days from the receipt of the request and the interpretation shall form part of the arbitral award.
A.P. No.98/2021 (3) The arbitral tribunal may correct any error of the type referred to in clause (a)
of sub-section (1), on its own initiative, within thirty days from the date of the arbitral award.

(4) Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, a party with notice to the other party, may request,
within thirty days from the receipt of the arbitral award, the arbitral tribunal to make an additional arbitral award as to claims presented in the arbitral proceedings but omitted from the arbitral award.
(5) If the arbitral tribunal considers the request made under sub-section (4) to be justified, it shall make the additional arbitral award within sixty days from the receipt of such request.

(6) The arbitral tribunal may extend, if necessary, the period of time within which it shall make a correction, give an interpretation or make an additional arbitral award under sub-section (2) or sub-section (5).
(7) Section 31 shall apply to a correction or interpretation of the arbitral award or to an additional arbitral award made under this section."
The aforesaid provision of law makes it clear that within 30 days from the date of receipt of Arbitral Award, a party with due notice to the other party, may request the Arbitral Tribunal to correct any computation errors, any clerical or typographical errors or any other errors of A.P. No.98/2021 a similar nature occurring in the award as well as the parties to the Arbitration proceedings with due notice to the other party may request the Arbitral Tribunal give an interpretation of a specific point or part of the award.

If any such application is within 30 days from the date of receipt of the order,

sentences.text: the Tribunal may consider the request and pass such order which become part of Arbitral Award.
Therefore, the aforesaid provision of law makes it clear that with due notice to the other side, any party can apply for a correction or interpretation of the arbitral award or part of the award.

In such application, the Arbitral Tribunal has every right to pass the award making corrections or interpretation of the award and that will form part of award.
.21.
As already discussed earlier in the case, the dispute has been arisen between the parties subsequent to passing of correction or    dated 05.01.2021.

In the case on hand undisputed, admitted and well settled principle of law is that the land looser is entitled for interest on the compensation amount is from A.P. No.98/2021 the date of loosing or handing over the possession of acquired property.

Thee Arbitrator/respondent No.2 in the award also made it clear at para No.3 of the operative portion of the award at page No.5 at last paragraph that the the petitioner shall pay the interest at the rate of 9% on the compensation amount from the date of taking possession till depositing of the compensation amount.

Subsequently the respondent No.2/
Arbitrator clarified the date of handing over the possession is 30.03.2004 vide order dated 05.01.2021.
It is equally important to note that the said rectification has been made by the respondent No.2 on the basis of reply given by the Project Director of the petitioner.
Absolutely there is no material on record to disbelieve that the possession of the acquired property has not been taken on 30.03.2004.

Further the petitioner has not produced any material before the court to show that the respondent No.1 continued with the possession of property even after 30.03.2004 till the receipt of compensation as on 30.06.2011.

Therefore the material on record only A.P. No.98/2021 suggest that the respondent No.1 lost the possession of property as on 30.03.2004 and on that the petitioner has taken the possession of the property of the petitioner hence this petitioner is liable to pay interest on the compensation amount from 30.03.2004 till depositing of the compensation amount as ordered in the corrigendum dated 05.01.2021.
.22.

Other contentions raised by the petitioner during the course of arguments is not discussed or considered as the petitioner has accepted the enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Arbitral Tribunal in its order dated 09.03.2020.
Therefore, viewed from any angle, this Court is not find any ground to intervene with the order of the tribunal and said order certainly in accordance with the law.

Therefore, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has failed to make out grounds to intervene with the award passed by the tribunal and the said ground is in accordance with law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case.

Accordingly, the above point is A.P.
No.98/2021 answered in the negative and proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the Corrigendum dated 05.01.2021 passed by the respondent No. 2 in case No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/07/2011-12 pertaining to Sy. No.24/3 measuring 4 guntas, Sy. No. 24/4 measuring 25 guntas and Sy. No. 24/5 measuring 12 guntas, totally measuring to an extent of 1 acre 1 gunta of land situated at Byatarayanapura village, Bengaluru North Taluka, regarding the payment of interest from 30-03-2004 on the compensation is hereby confirmed.

opennyai_summary.facts: The respondent No.1 received the said amount under protest and filed an A.P. No.98/2021 application for enhancing proper and fair compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petitioner claims that the respondents 1 and 2 have violated the provision of Section 33(1)(a) of the Arbitration and A.P.
No.98/2021 entertained the application of respondent No.1 contrary to the legal provisions and against the principles of natural justice.
The learned advocate for the petitioner relied on the judgments reported in (1) AIR 2020 SC 717 - The Executive Engineer, Nimna Dundha Project Vs. the State of Maharastra and others;
(2) AIE 2003 Karnataka page 165; (3) ILR 1985 Karnataka (SC) page 1261; (3)
2004(7) KLJ page 100; (4) MANU/UP/1383/2004 in the case of Divakar Rai Sharma Vs. Ashish Kumar Singh and Dharamveer Singh and (5) Oil and Natural Gas Corp.
Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd (AIR 2003 SC 2629).
opennyai_summary.issue:
"Whether the Corrigendum / additional impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?"
.8.
.11. In the case on hand, the parties to the proceedings are not disputing that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation from the date of handing over of the possession of the acquired property till depositing of the amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No. 2 arbitrator in the award granted the compensation by ordering to pay the interest on the compensation at the rate of 9% from the date of handing over the possession of the acquired land till deposit of the amount to the petitioner.
.12. The award passed by the respondent No.2 at para No. 3 only disclose that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest from the date of handing over the possession of acquired property to the petitioner.
Hence, the court has to find out which is the date in which possession of the property has been handed over to the authority of the acquired land.
Hence, claimed that the respondent No. 1 is entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation only from 30.06.2011 and not from 2004 as ordered in the impugned corrigendum.
.13.
In the said application, the respondent No. 1 made out a case that it has received the compensation on 30.06.2011 and the work has been completed in the year 2005 itself and the respondent No.1 is entitled for compensation with interest from the date of taking of possession as per Section 3(h)(5) of NHAI Act.
Therefore, the award has been passed on 30.03.2004, but the compensation was disbursed on 30.06.2011 and as on that date, the land loser approached with documents.
Hence, it is clear that till 30.06.2011 the land loser / respondent No. 1 not appeared before the petitioner and on that date, while making the payment, the signatures of the respondent No. 1 has been obtained on the documents.
Except Annexure-E, there is nothing on record to show that the possession of the property has been handed over to the petitioner as on 30.06.2011.
If at all the possession of the acquired property has been handed over to the petitioner as on 30.06.2011, it is practically impossible for the petitioner to commence the formation of road work in the year 2004 National Highways Authority Of India vs M/S Ministry Of Communications ... on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112216299/
6 and complete the same in the year 2005.
Further the burden is on the petitioner to show that when actually they have taken possession of the property.
The petitioner is failed to make out a specific case of taking possession of property.
Under such circumstances, the Court can safely infer that the date of award itself is the date of taking of possession of the acquired property.
.18. It is well settled principle of law that the land looser is entitled for compensation with interest from the date of handing over the possession.
Therefore, the aforesaid provision of law makes it clear that with due notice to the other side, any party can apply for a correction or interpretation of the arbitral award or part of the award.
In such application, the Arbitral Tribunal has every right to pass the award making corrections or interpretation of the award and that will form part of award.
.21.
In the case on hand undisputed, admitted and well settled principle of law is that the land looser is entitled for interest on the compensation amount is from A.P. No.98/2021 the date of loosing or handing over the possession of acquired property.
Absolutely there is no material on record to disbelieve that the possession of the acquired property has not been taken on 30.03.2004.
Therefore the material on record only A.P. No.98/2021 suggest that the respondent No.1 lost the possession of property as on 30.03.2004 and on that the petitioner has taken the possession of the property of the petitioner hence this petitioner is liable to pay interest on the compensation amount from 30.03.2004 till depositing of the compensation amount as ordered in the corrigendum dated 05.01.2021.
.22.
